newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit hits five-mth low on month-end dlr demand.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit hits five-mth low on month-end dlr demand.

text.p: The ringgit hit a five-month low on the dollar's strength and month-end Malaysian commercial demand for foreign currency, dealers said.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5070/77 per dollar against 2.5013/20 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Wednesday. It hit a five-month low of 2.5080 an hour earlier.
Dealers said some dollar sales by Malaysian exporters failed to halt the ringgit's slide.
"Although exporters tried to cap ringgit losses at 2.5052 and 2.5060, buying interests for the U.S. dollar were certainly more forceful," research firm I.D.E.A said in a statement.

It said even profit-taking by offshore players could not stop the slide of the ringgit. "Unless the U.S. dollar/yen challenge the 111-yen resistance seriously, further losses are not expected on the ringgit," it added.

One analyst said there may be some return of foreign funds to the ringgit by next week as Malaysian interest rates are expected to rebound after a two billion ringgit government bond issue, which would soak up the market's excess liquidity.
"Funds will return to the ringgit from Singapore for yield play," he said.
